title: Scientific model and provenance
scope: An educational well-mixed stochastic reaction model with sampled Brownian positions in a representative serotonergic contact. Molecular geometry is sourced; whole-neuron anatomy and transport-cycle motion are illustrative. It is not atomistic molecular dynamics or a prediction of individual treatment response.

notes.title: What escitalopram does
notes.text: Escitalopram binds the central substrate site of SERT and stabilizes an outward-open conformation, reducing serotonin reuptake. It does not plug a serotonin receptor, manufacture serotonin, or covalently bind the transporter.

notes.title: Real structures, explicit protonation
notes.text: Molecule views use PubChem computed 3D conformers with all hydrogens: escitalopram⁺ (C20H22FN2O⁺) and serotonin⁺ (C10H13N2O⁺). They are single conformers, not fixed shapes of flexible molecules in water. Escitalopram’s S configuration was independently checked from coordinates.

notes.title: An experimental SERT snapshot
notes.text: The SERT detail uses chain A of PDB 5I71, a 3.15 Å X-ray structure of an engineered thermostabilized construct. The trace contains 542 Cα positions plus the actual bound escitalopram heavy-atom pose. Cartoon gate motion is schematic.

notes.title: What the moving particles mean
notes.text: Binding follows exact Gillespie well-mixed kinetics. Reflected Brownian positions are sampled every 0.01 s; sub-microsecond crossings between samples are unresolved. Visual paths are explanatory, and binding is based on pooled concentration, not on rendered collisions.

notes.title: A local burst in a tiny volume
notes.text: The model box is 200 × 20 × 130 nm. One explicit serotonin molecule corresponds to 3.193344 µM in that volume; 120 initial molecules represent about 383 µM locally. This is not a bulk brain concentration. Free escitalopram is a separate nM reservoir.

notes.title: Transport is coupled to ions
notes.text: SERT uptake depends on sodium and chloride gradients maintained by cellular metabolism. A transporter is an alternating-access carrier, not a permanently open pore. The reduced model assumes maintained ion gradients and does not integrate membrane voltage or individual transport ions.

notes.title: Serotonin changes receptor signaling
notes.text: Receptor activation is shown as occupancy, not a guaranteed postsynaptic action potential. Effects depend on receptor subtype and cell context. Released serotonin may diffuse beyond a single contact; a narrow synaptic cleft is a teaching geometry, not the anatomy of every serotonergic release site.

notes.title: The medicine’s salt is not the binding ligand
notes.text: Escitalopram is supplied as an oxalate salt. In solution, acid–base equilibria and dissociation apply; oxalate is not covalently attached to the drug. The optional oxalate structure is background chemistry and is not co-delivered as a simulated SERT-blocking species.

notes.title: Seconds and weeks are different models
notes.text: Synaptic diffusion and receptor occupancy cannot by themselves predict clinical benefit. A roughly 27–32 hour terminal half-life supports a separate day-scale pharmacokinetic illustration; plasma exposure is not the same quantity as free drug concentration at a synapse.

notes.title: Beyond the central binding site
notes.text: An extracellular allosteric escitalopram site has also been observed experimentally. The reduced central-site occupancy model does not attempt to infer the clinical contribution of that site.

equations.name: Overdamped Brownian diffusion
equations.note: Three independent Gaussian increments per step. D must match the length and time units. Water collisions are integrated out; ballistic Newtonian trajectories would be inappropriate at this coarse scale.

equations.name: First-order reaction probability
equations.note: k is a hazard in inverse time. Several mutually exclusive events require a combined hazard and conditional event choice, or an explicitly justified operator split.

equations.name: Drug occupancy
equations.expression: dθ/dt = kon[I](1−θ) − koffθ; θeq = [I]/([I]+Kd); Kd = koff/kon
equations.note: Applies to a simple reversible site under a fixed free-ligand reservoir. It does not mean that changing the total displayed particle count changes a calibrated tissue concentration.

equations.name: Competitive inhibition reference
equations.note: A reduced steady-state comparison under classical competitive assumptions, not a full SERT alternating-access and allosteric mechanism.

equations.name: Absorption and elimination
equations.note: For a single dose with ka≠ke in a one-compartment model. Repeated doses require summing shifted terms; this model does not describe brain concentration or clinical onset.

equations.name: Tetrahedral handedness audit
equations.note: The four neighbor positions must first be ordered by CIP priority. The sign is a coordinate integrity check; a determinant with arbitrary atom order does not by itself establish R/S.

limitations: Molecular display scale is enlarged relative to tissue; do not compare molecule radii and neuron diameters in the overview.
Soma, axon, dendrites, organelles and membranes are procedural teaching geometry, not a traced biological specimen.
No explicit solvent, electrostatic field, atomic force field, membrane potential, protein free-energy landscape, receptor second-messenger network, or complete neuronal circuit is integrated.
Binding rates, capture radii and receptor populations are configurable educational model parameters, not a fit to a human patient or dose.
SERT has more states and allosteric effects than the simplified inhibition model. A static experimental pose does not determine the transport pathway.
Statistical and numerical tests validate the implemented equations, conservation and molecular assets; they do not establish clinical predictive validity.
